title: Causal Coarse-Graining and the Almeida Growth Index: A Micro–Macro Research Program Within the Dead Universe Theory
content: The value γ_A = (√5 − 1)/2, established within the effective DUT formulation, is shown to be consistent with a distinct causal coarse-graining framework based on a two-channel, unit-multiplicity history architecture. Within this framework, the causal-history dynamics generate a structural constraint compatible with γ_A. Within the two-channel integer-multiplicity family, (p,q)=(1,1) is further shown to be the unique discrete architecture compatible with the previously established DUT value γ_A, establishing algebraic uniqueness within this causal class. This consistency supports the interpretation of γ_A as a robust structural parameter of causal coarse-graining rather than a model-specific artifact. We develop a unified analysis based on the non-minimally coupled scalar action, exact compactification of z = ξS², slow–fast reduction, exact second-order response theory, minimal state-space realization, and Mori–Zwanzig projection. The exact transformation O = z/(1 + z), D = 1/(1 + z) implies D/O = 1/z. The microscopic response possesses a minimal two-dimensional realization and, away from critical damping, two distinct simple physical poles. Exact temporal sampling proves that the signed local scalar amplitude does not coincide with the positive history-counting variable, while projection onto the relevant scalar–curvature observable yields the explicit memory kernel K(t) = PLQ · e^(QLQt) · QLP; for the locally stationary damped realization this reduces to K(t) = −ω² · e^(−Γt), with effective projected resolvent G_eff(s) = (s + Γ)/(s² + Γs + ω²). The causal-history architecture is represented by two exhaustive, disjoint unit-cardinality extension classes, giving p = q = 1 and hence N_n = N_(n−1) + N_(n−2). The resulting ratio map R_(n+1) = 1/(1 + R_n) has the unique positive stable fixed point R_* = (√5 − 1)/2. Identifying the asymptotic ordered fraction with this scale-invariant ratio yields D/O = O and maps exactly to z_c = (1 + √5)/2. The resulting prediction γ_A = 0.618034 is fixed before observational comparison and is directly testable with Euclid, DESI, and CSST growth data.
